what_happened: We measured the tone of the voice in three parts: body in the low band, brightness, and air at the top. Brightness and air were inside what real recordings show. Body was far outside: the voice carried too much low end and competed with the kick. A low shelf cut on the voice alone brought body inside, and nothing else had to change.
lesson: Check tone in parts before changing anything. Ours had one fault, too much low end in the voice, and one cut fixed it; the bright end was already fine.

evidence.claim: Body on real hip hop voices runs -8.30 to 2.76 dB (5th to 95th percentile, median -2.11); ours read 7.79 dB
Tilt (-13.61 dB), air (-21.93 dB) and flatness (0.04) on our render were inside the real ranges
After a 12 dB low shelf cut at 250 Hz body read 1.83 dB, measured on the clean voice only
Seven of eight planted tone checks pass; movement of tone over time fails and is not used
